class.name: SafeGDScript
class.brief_description: A script written in GDScript, compiled to RISC-V and executed inside a [Sandbox].
class.description:
A script written in GDScript and saved with the [code].sgd[/code] extension. The script is compiled to a RISC-V program and executed inside a [Sandbox]. It extends the functionality of the objects that instantiate it in the same way a [GDScript] does: exported properties, signals, [method Node._ready] and the other engine callbacks all work the same. The difference is that the code can only access what the sandbox allows. Ordinary GDScript compiles unchanged, so the rest of this description only covers what SafeGDScript adds. Each addition also comes with a script template. Choose SafeGDScript in the [b]Create Script[/b] dialog and pick [i]GDScript Tour[/i], [i]Typed Struct[/i], [i]Nullable and Union Types[/i], [i]If Var[/i], or [i]Traits[/i]. [b]Structs[/b] A [code]struct[/code] is a [Dictionary] with a fixed set of fields. Godot and GDScript see an ordinary [Dictionary], but the compiler knows the fields: accessing a field that the struct does not declare is a compile error instead of a new key, and field access compiles to a direct lookup. Fields can be typed and given default values. A struct can also declare constants and functions. [codeblock] struct Particle: var position: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO var velocity: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO var lifetime: float = 1.0
func advance(delta: float) -> bool: self.position += self.velocity * delta self.lifetime -= delta return self.lifetime > 0.0
func spawn() -> void: var a := Particle.new() # Every field has its default value. var b := Particle(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(50, -80)) # Positional, in declaration order. var c := Particle(lifetime = 2.5, velocity = Vector2(-30, -60)) # Named. Skipped fields keep their defaults. [/codeblock] A struct is a value, so a variable or field declared with a struct type starts as a new instance instead of [code]null[/code]. A [code]match[/code] pattern can destructure a struct by position or by name. Every field must appear in the pattern. [codeblock] match point: Point(x = var a, y = 0): return a # Points on the X axis. Point(var a, _): return a [/codeblock] [b]Traits[/b] A [code]trait[/code] holds state and behavior that scripts, inner classes, and structs can share. A script uses traits with a [code]uses[/code] statement at the top of the file, and an inner class puts [code]uses[/code] in its header. The trait's variables, functions, constants, and enums become part of everything that uses it. A trait function without a body is abstract. Anything that uses the trait must implement it, otherwise compilation fails. If a user declares a function with the same name as a trait function, the trait's version remains available as [code]TraitName.method()[/code]. [codeblock] uses Damageable
trait Damageable: var health: int = 100
func take_damage(amount: int) -> void: health -= amount if health <= 0: on_death()
func on_death() -> void # Abstract, since it has no body.
func on_death() -> void: queue_free()
class Crate uses Damageable: func on_death() -> void: print("Crate splinters")
func hit_all(targets: Array, amount: int) -> void: for target in targets: if target is Damageable: target.take_damage(amount) [/codeblock] A trait is also a type. [code]value is Damageable[/code] is [code]true[/code] for anything that uses the trait, and for any object that has every function the trait declares, so an engine object or a GDScript instance can satisfy a trait at run time. See also [method uses_trait]. A trait can use other traits. A trait can be placed in its own file starting with [code]trait_name MyTrait[/code], which other scripts then refer to as [code]uses MyTrait[/code]. If a file with a [code]class_name[/code] declares several traits, they are used one at a time: [code]uses Library.Alpha, Library.Beta[/code]. [b]switch[/b] [code]switch[/code] is a [code]match[/code] that is guaranteed to compile to a jump table, so selecting a branch takes the same time no matter how many branches there are. The value must be a known [int] and every pattern must be a constant integer, except for the [code]_[/code] wildcard. A duplicate pattern, a value of unknown type, a pattern that is not an integer constant, a [code]when[/code] guard, or values too far apart for a table are compile errors. The error message names the rule that was broken. [codeblock] switch state: State.IDLE: wait() State.RUNNING: step() _: push_error("Unhandled state") [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] A [code]match[/code] with the same shape also compiles to a jump table, and falls back to a chain of comparisons if it cannot. [b]when[/b] Any [code]match[/code] branch can have a [code]when[/code] guard, which is evaluated after the pattern matches. If the guard is [code]false[/code], matching continues with the next branch instead of leaving the [code]match[/code] statement. Because of this, a guarded [code]_[/code] does not catch everything. [codeblock] match event: {"kind": "hit", "amount": var amount, ..} when amount > 0: take_damage(amount) {"kind": "hit", ..}: pass # A hit for nothing. _: push_warning("Unknown event") [/codeblock] [b]Union types[/b] A union type [code]A | B[/code] accepts a value of any of the listed types. Unions can be used on local variables, member variables, parameters, return types, signals, and struct fields. The variable still holds a single [Variant]. Assignments the compiler can see are checked at compile time, and any other assignment is checked once at run time. Using [code]is[/code], comparing with [code]null[/code], testing truthiness, matching on values, or matching on [code]typeof(x)[/code] narrows the union, so the code in that branch is compiled for the narrowed type. [code]x is int | String[/code] is a single test. [codeblock] func describe(key: int | String) -> String: if key is int: return "id #%d" % key # key is an int here. return "named '%s'" % key # key is a String here.
func find_by(key: int | String) -> Node?: match typeof(key): TYPE_INT: return get_child(key) if key < get_child_count() else null TYPE_STRING: return get_node_or_null(key) return null [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] The engine has no union type, so union parameters, return values, and properties appear as [Variant] to Godot. [b]Nullable types[/b] [code]T?[/code] can be used wherever a type hint can, and means [code]T | null[/code]. A nullable variable without an initial value starts as [code]null[/code]. Comparing with [code]null[/code], [code]is[/code], [code]assert[/code], and the right side of [code]and[/code] narrow the variable to [code]T[/code] for the rest of that branch. [code]a?.b[/code] and [code]a?.method()[/code] evaluate to [code]null[/code] if [code]a[/code] is [code]null[/code], without performing the access. [code]a ?? b[/code] evaluates to [code]a[/code] unless it is [code]null[/code], in which case [code]b[/code] is evaluated and returned. [codeblock] var target: Node? = null
func _process(_delta: float) -> void: if target != null and not target.is_inside_tree(): target = null # target is known to be a Node in the condition above.
func label() -> String: return target?.name ?? "(nothing)" [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] [code]if value:[/code] only narrows the [code]true[/code] branch. Values such as [code]0[/code], an empty [String], and [constant Vector2.ZERO] are falsy without being [code]null[/code]. [b]if var[/b] [code]if var name = expression:[/code] evaluates the expression once and enters the block only if the result is not [code]null[/code]. Inside the block, the variable is known to be non-null. The variable is only visible in the [code]if[/code] block, not in [code]else[/code] and not after the statement. Both [code]:=[/code] and an explicit type hint work. With a type hint, a non-null value must be of that type. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: if var player := get_node_or_null("Player"): print("Found ", player.name) else: print("No Player yet")
if var volume: float = settings.get("volume"): print("Volume is %.1f" % volume)
func first_visible(nodes: Array) -> CanvasItem?: for candidate in nodes: if var item := candidate as CanvasItem: if item.visible: return item return null [/codeblock] [b]Lua-style dictionaries[/b] A [Dictionary] literal can use bare names as keys, and a dictionary key can be read with a dot as well as with brackets. [codeblock] var player := {name = "Bob", age = 30} # Same as {"name": "Bob", "age": 30}. print(player.name, " is ", player["age"]) # Prints "Bob is 30" [/codeblock] [b]@test[/b] The [code]@test[/code] annotation marks a function without parameters as a test. The function remains an ordinary method, and is additionally published as a test. Each test runs on a new instance of the script, so member variables have their default values and [method Object._init] runs again. The instance is never added to the scene tree, so [method Node._ready], [method Node._enter_tree], and [method Node._process] are not called and [code]$Child[/code] is [code]null[/code]. A test passes if it returns normally. A failed [code]assert[/code], a sandbox exception, or a loop that exceeds the instruction limit fails the test. [codeblock] @test func a_particle_expires_after_its_lifetime(): var p := Particle(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(10, 0), 0.5) assert(p.advance(0.25), "Still alive halfway through") assert(not p.advance(0.25), "Gone once the lifetime runs out") assert(p.position.x == 5.0) [/codeblock] To run the tests of a script, right-click a [code].sgd[/code] file in the FileSystem dock, a node in the Scene dock, or the script in the script editor. You can also call [method run_tests] from a tool script, or [method SafeGDScriptLanguage.run_tests] to run several scripts at once. To run tests from the command line, for example in CI, use the headless runner: [codeblock lang=text] godot --headless --path . -s addons/godot_sandbox/run_sgd_tests.gd [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] Tests are not included in exported projects. See [method compile_shipping].

method.name: clear_breakpoints
method.description: Removes all breakpoints and recompiles the script. Returns [code]false[/code] if the recompilation failed.

method.name: compile_shipping
method.description: Recompiles the script the way an exported project does: without profiling, debug information, or [code]@test[/code] functions. Returns [code]false[/code] on a compile error, which [method get_compile_error] then describes.

method.name: debug_continue
method.description: Resumes the script that is stopped at a breakpoint. Does nothing if no script is stopped.

method.name: editor_documentation
method.description: Returns the documentation pages this script publishes to the editor's help, one for each class, struct, and trait it declares. [b]Note:[/b] This method is used internally by the engine and is exposed for testing.

method.name: editor_member_line
method.description: Returns the line [param member] is declared on, starting from [code]1[/code], or [code]-1[/code] if the script does not declare it. [b]Note:[/b] This method is used internally by the engine and is exposed for testing.

method.name: get_active_breakpoints
method.description: Returns the lines the current build placed a breakpoint on, in ascending order. A line without code of its own gets no breakpoint.

method.name: get_breakpoints
method.description: Returns the requested breakpoint lines in ascending order, whether or not the build could place them. See also [method get_active_breakpoints].

method.name: get_compile_error
method.description: Returns the error message of the last failed compilation, or an empty [String] if the script compiled successfully.

method.name: get_content
method.description: Returns the compiled RISC-V ELF program.

method.name: get_stopped_backtrace
method.description: Returns the call stack of the script that is stopped at a breakpoint, innermost frame first. Returns an empty array if no script is stopped.

method.name: get_stopped_line
method.description: Returns the line the stopped script is waiting on, or [code]-1[/code] if no script is stopped.

method.name: get_test_functions
method.description: Returns the names of the functions marked with [code]@test[/code], in declaration order.

method.name: get_test_lines
method.description: Returns the declaration line of each function in [method get_test_functions], starting from [code]1[/code], in the same order.

method.name: get_translation_hash
method.description: Returns the hash identifying this script's program and its translation options, or [code]0[/code] if no program is loaded. See also [method Sandbox.get_translation_hash].

method.name: is_debug_build
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the current build contains debug information, that is, a line table and a shadow stack. Breakpoints and backtraces require debug information.

method.name: is_profiled_build
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the current build was compiled with profiling enabled. See also [method set_profiling].

method.name: is_stopped
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a SafeGDScript is stopped at a breakpoint. Only one script can be stopped at a time.

method.name: new
method.description: Returns a new instance of the script. The arguments are passed to its [method Object._init]. [codeblock] var MyClass = load("my_class.sgd") var instance = MyClass.new() print(instance.get_script() == MyClass) # Prints true [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] A script that declares a trait cannot be instantiated.

method.name: poll_base_sources
method.description: Recompiles every loaded script whose base script changed on disk. The editor calls this periodically. A running game does not need to.

method.name: run_tests
method.description: Runs the script's [code]@test[/code] functions, each on a new instance, and returns the results: [codeblock lang=text] { "path": "res://player.sgd", "passed": 3, "failed": 1, "errors": 0, "elapsed_usec": 812, "tests": [ { "name": "health_is_clamped", "line": 7, "status": "passed", "message": "", "elapsed_usec": 210 }, { "name": "members_start_at_defaults", "line": 12, "status": "failed", "message": "Sandbox exception in AssertionError: ...", "location": "res://player.sgd:14", "elapsed_usec": 190 }, ] } [/codeblock] [code]status[/code] is [code]"passed"[/code], [code]"failed"[/code] if the test raised an error, or [code]"error"[/code] if the test could not run at all because of a compile error, a refused instance, or an invalid call. If [param only] is not empty, only the named tests run. An unknown name is reported as an [code]"error"[/code] row. If [param quiet] is [code]true[/code], failures are not printed and only the returned [Dictionary] reports them.

method.name: set_breakpoint
method.description: Adds or removes a breakpoint on [param line], starting from [code]1[/code], and recompiles the script. Breakpoints are compiled into the program and cost nothing when unset. Returns [code]false[/code] if the recompilation failed. The requested breakpoints are kept either way. [b]Note:[/b] A script that is stopped at a breakpoint cannot be recompiled.

method.name: set_breakpoints
method.description: Replaces all breakpoints with [param lines] and recompiles the script once. Returns [code]false[/code] if the recompilation failed.

method.name: set_profiling
method.description: Enables or disables profiling and recompiles the script. Returns [code]false[/code] if the recompilation failed.

method.name: uses_trait
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this script, or a script it extends, uses the trait called [param name]. [b]Note:[/b] Unlike [code]is TraitName[/code] inside SafeGDScript, this method does not consider an object that merely has all of the trait's functions.

signal.name: breakpoint_hit
signal.description: Emitted when execution reaches a breakpoint. A connected listener takes priority over the editor's own stop, and is responsible for resuming the script with [method debug_continue].
